title: Centered half-turn of a partially baked pizza with a turning peel
objective: Using YAM and a representative full-scale turning peel, rotate a roughly 300 mm partially baked pizza approximately 180 degrees on the stone inside a closed-roof 16-inch-class oven. Bring the visibly pale rim sector toward the modeled hot side while keeping the pizza near its initial center, top-side-up, supported, and inside the oven throughout; then withdraw the peel completely. Cooking chemistry and food safety are outside scope.
skills: thin-blade insertion beneath a compliant crust rim
guarded lifting to reduce deck friction
tangential traction and in-plane yaw control
success_conditions: Use native pose and contact traces plus video. Full credit: absolute yaw change 150–210 degrees; maximum center excursion throughout the trial no more than 50 mm; final center displacement no more than 35 mm; pizza continuously supported by stone, peel, or both; pizza remains top-side-up and entirely inside the oven; peel finishes fully clear. Partial credit: yaw change 90–149 degrees; maximum trajectory excursion no more than 80 mm; final displacement no more than 60 mm; all support, containment, orientation, release, and damage conditions still satisfied. Zero credit otherwise, including gripper contact with pizza, removing it to rotate, any interval without stone-or-peel support, overturning, pose writes, welds, unreleased peel contact, crust penetration, permanent rim folding outside the validated compliance range, topping separation, a fall, or damaging robot/tool/oven collision. The pale sector is visible corroboration, not a substitute for measured yaw.
industrial_value: Represents the repeated in-oven turning operation used to expose different pizza sectors to uneven heat without extracting the food. It evaluates confined food-service tool manipulation rather than the rejected miniature launch task.
dexterity: High: the robot must acquire and steer a long tool, insert a thin blade under a compliant edge, modulate normal force, generate controlled tangential traction, limit translation of a weakly supported food object, and release it cleanly through a restricted oven mouth.

asset_plan: Create an independently authored representative fixture rather than claiming an exact product replica: a closed-roof 16-inch-class oven with a nominal 406 mm pizza capacity, a 300 mm pizza, and a small circular perforated turning-peel head on a long handle. Treat mouth height, deck depth, blade thickness, masses, friction, and stiffness as disclosed provisional settings. Model the set underside/core as rigid and use only a shallow validated compliant rim/contact approximation; toppings may be visually integrated but must not create hidden grasp geometry. Before full-demo development, run separate current-trial native tests for YAM grasp acquisition, full-scale handle reach, roof and mouth clearance, blade insertion, tangential traction, continuous support, release, and withdrawal. Use ordinary guarded YAM joint and gripper actions only, with no task-object pose control, weld, collision disabling, or scale reduction.
risk: The dominant risks are insufficient full-scale reach, handle or wrist collision at the oven mouth, blade tunneling, excessive stone friction, unrealistic rim compliance, and poor yaw observability. A visible asymmetric browning marker resolves yaw ambiguity without changing collision or mass. Any failed reach, clearance, insertion, traction, support, or release gate blocks the full demonstration rather than permitting smaller equipment or hidden constraints.
